properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research on the emerging "graph brain around the codebase" ecosystem, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. STILL OPEN.

WHAT THE SURVEY SHOWS. The field has converged on two families, and reflow2 is in neither:

(1) CODE-AS-GRAPH — Graphify, Understand Anything, Sourcegraph/Cody. The graph is DERIVED from the code by static analysis plus LLM summarisation. It answers "what depends on this", "what breaks if I change this function".

(2) AGENT MEMORY — Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta (MemGPT), Cognee, Supermemory, LangMem, LlamaIndex Memory. The graph is DERIVED from conversation and execution traces. It answers "what did we say before", "what worked last time".

THE READING OFFERED, and it is the agent's own analysis rather than anything Alex or the research says: both families are DESCRIPTIVE, and the property they therefore cannot have is disagreement. A graph re-derived from the code can never contradict the code — if the code drifts from intent, the graph drifts with it and reports nothing. A memory layer never contradicts anything either; it recalls. reflow2's graph is AUTHORED and sits UPSTREAM of the code, which is what lets it say the code is wrong: drift, gaps, defects, unrealized capabilities, a failing gate. That is not a feature the survey's tools lack by oversight — it is unavailable to anything whose graph is a function of the artifact.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is a design question and not a marketing one: if that is the line reflow2 defends, several current tensions resolve one way rather than the other. Retrieval quality (dec:idea-embeddings-adoption) becomes a convenience rather than the product. The gates, drift detection and the coherence loop become the core rather than the overhead. And "reflow2 as a memory layer you sprinkle on" becomes the wrong shape, because a layer that plugs into somebody else's agent framework has no standing to refuse. Conversely, if the line is NOT defended, the honest conclusion may be that several of these tools already do most of what a user wants at a fraction of the adoption cost.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: every tool in the survey is a LAYER — it plugs into LangGraph/LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel or Claude Code, and the user keeps everything else they had. reflow2 is a whole system: its own store, schema, skill kit, gates and vocabulary. Being normative is exactly WHY it cannot be a thin layer, so the differentiator and the adoption cost are the same fact seen twice. req:thin-install and req:frictionless-update are pushing on this, and a one-line install does not by itself make a coherence loop cheap to adopt. Whether there is a legitimate smaller entry point — read-only, query-only, no loop — or whether that entry point would be a dishonest version of the product, is part of what is open here.

WHAT IS ALSO WORTH NOTING AND IS NOT A QUESTION: Sourcegraph exposing its graph to agents over MCP is the pattern reflow2 already implements. That is validation, not a gap. Mem0's "organizational memory" tier (knowledge many agents share) is the same territory as req:many-designs-one-service and dec:central-host, which are already in flight — also validation.
properties.name: OPEN — is reflow2's differentiator that the graph can be RIGHT when the code is WRONG, and what should follow from defending that line?
properties.rationale: Recorded because there is currently NO node anywhere in the design that says what reflow2 is that comparable tools are not, and a differentiator nobody wrote down cannot be defended when a build decision quietly trades it away. The specific value of the survey is that it is the first external evidence of what the alternatives actually do, so the comparison is against real systems rather than a supposed rival.
